paper.title_en: Introducing Parton-Level Fluctuations in the TRENTo-Sea Model
paper.abstract_en: A variety of experimental and theoretical data suggest that initial condition models for heavy-ion collisions contain a degree of sub-nucleonic fluctuations. While current models fit the number and size of these fluctuations to data, we use nuclear parton distribution functions to constrain sub-nucleonic structure and fluctuations in TRENTo-Sea, an extension of TRENTo. Sampling the momentum fraction distributions of quarks and gluons in heavy ions, we use perturbative quantum chromodynamics to collide nuclei at the parton level, and we introduce an infrared center-of-momentum damping scale which is tuned to proton-proton cross sections. We find that our model successfully reproduces the $\varepsilon_2\{2\}$ of data-calibrated models except in central collisions, and an analysis of the power spectrum and granularity of the pre-equilibrium fireball shows that the number of low-$x$ partons in a nucleon has a significant effect on the local transverse geometry. Our model is largely insensitive to variations of the infrared parameters, as such changes are absorbed into the calibration of the infrared regulator. We expect that this work will aid future research on soft-hard correlations and constraining different nPDF sets.
